messages.author: 13b6ace5063d6653
messages.subject: Very large number of markers
parts:
Good morning,

I'd like to hear about your strategies to deal with datasets containing very large numbers of markers. 

One approach is to first eliminate duplicates, but one question I have respectful to that is, if there is plenty of missing data, which strategy to search for duplicates should be adopted?

All the best,
Mathias

messages.author: 13b6ace5063d6653
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Very large number of markers
parts:
Hi Karl,

I realize that I was not clear at all, sorry. I am trying to figure out what would be the best way to form linkage groups from a dataset with around 45,000 markers, in a population of the ri self or f2 intercross type (typically 200 individuals). The problem is that our datasets (GBS) usually contain plenty of missing data (ranging from 25 to 65 %), so I can't see how findDupMarkers and find duplicates efficiently. 

Also, the markers are not ordered a priori since we don't have a reference genome. 

My understanding is that in R/qtl it is necessary to compute the LOD score/recombination fraction matrix before forming the linkage groups. And on my machine (64 bit, 16 GB RAM), this take a so huge amount of RAM that R starts swapping on the hard drive and I expect this to last for ages (I calculated that the LOD/recombination fraction matrix' size would be around 65 GB).

So I was wondering if it would be possible to form the linkage groups without computing the entire matrix, for example, one could compute only the recombination fraction and LOD score for the tested pair of markers.

Does this make sense to you?

Thanks very much for the support. 

All the best,
Mathias

It's straightforward what to do, to avoid that, but it would be a bit of work; I'll add it to my "to do" list.

karl
